name: What to Expect During a Bathroom Renovation Project

step.name: Step 1: Plan the scope and secure necessary building permits
step.text: Meet with your contractor to finalize layout drawings, verify plumbing and electrical upgrades, choose materials, and submit building plans to your local jurisdiction before starting any physical work.

step.name: Step 2: Complete careful demolition and framing inspection
step.text: Crews remove old tile, fixtures, and wallboards down to the studs, allowing builders to inspect the underlying framing and subfloor for concealed water damage or wood rot before proceeding.

step.name: Step 3: Execute rough mechanical, plumbing, and electrical trade work
step.text: Licensed trades reposition drain lines, run new water supplies, set up dedicated circuits for lighting and outlets, and install proper exhaust ducting to meet regional building codes.

step.name: Step 4: Install code-compliant waterproofing and wall surfaces
step.text: Install moisture-resistant backer board, apply continuous waterproofing membranes across shower pans and wet areas, and hang drywall across the remaining walls and ceiling.

step.name: Step 5: Lay tile, set primary fixtures, and finish surfaces
step.text: Tile artisans install floor and wall finishes, grout the joints, position the vanity and countertop, and connect the toilet, faucets, and shower fixtures once surfaces cure.

step.name: Step 6: Complete final testing and walk through the punch list
step.text: Turn on all plumbing fixtures to test drainage and pressure, check electrical switches and ventilation airflow, and review the detailed punch list to confirm every finishing touch is done.
